pr_title: fix(security): enforce management-plane isolation for API tokens, fix team scoping, and fix blocked usage logging
problem_statement:
# Bug-fix PR
## Summary

Fixes three security bugs in the API token lifecycle: token management endpoints could be accessed using API tokens (privilege escalation), team membership was not auto-inherited when creating tokens (broken scoping), and blocked/revoked token usage was never logged (invisible audit trail).

---

## Related Issue
Closes: #3291 

---

## Root Cause

### Bug 1 — Token Chaining (Privilege Escalation)
`_require_authenticated_session()` only blocked anonymous (unauthenticated) requests. It did not check `auth_method`, so an API token bearer could call `POST /tokens`, `GET /tokens`, `DELETE /tokens/{id}`, etc. — allowing an API token to create or revoke other tokens.

### Bug 2 — Broken Team Inheritance
`create_token()` attempted to auto-populate `team_id` from the caller's team membership using `current_user.get("teams")`. However, `get_current_user_with_permissions()` (in `rbac.py`) injects teams into the user dict under the key `token_teams` — not `teams`. The lookup always returned `None`, so non-admin users who omitted `team_id` always created globally-scoped tokens regardless of their team membership.

### Bug 3a — `blocked` Flag Always False
`token_usage_middleware.py` hardcoded `blocked=False` when logging authenticated API token requests, regardless of the actual HTTP response status code.

### Bug 3b — Revoked/Expired Token Attempts Not Logged
When a revoked or expired API token was rejected (HTTP 401/403), the middleware exited early because `request.state.auth_method` is never set for failed auth. These attempts were silently dropped with no audit trail.

---

## Fix Description

### `mcpgateway/routers/tokens.py`

**Bug 1:** Added an explicit `auth_method == "api_token"` check inside `_require_authenticated_session()`, which is called at the top of all 11 token management endpoints:

```python
if auth_method == "api_token":
    raise HTTPException(
        status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
        detail=(
            "Token management requires an interactive session (JWT from web login or SSO). "
            "API tokens cannot create, list, or revoke other tokens."
        ),
    )
```

**Bug 2:** Replaced the broken `.get("teams")` lookup with `.get("token_teams")` and introduced an `effective_team_id` variable with fallback logic for single-team non-admin users. Admin tokens remain globally scoped (`team_id=null`).

### `mcpgateway/middleware/token_usage_middleware.py`

**Bug 3a:** Replaced `blocked=False` hardcode with `blocked = status_code >= 400`.

**Bug 3b:** Added a new `elif status_code in (401, 403)` branch that uses `jwt.decode(..., options={"verify_signature": False})` to identify whether the rejected bearer token was an API token, then logs it with `blocked=True` and the appropriate `block_reason` (`"revoked_or_expired"` for 401, `"http_403"` for 403).

---

## Verification

| Bug | Test Method | Expected | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — Token Chaining | `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <api_token>" POST /tokens` | HTTP 403 | ✅ |
| 2 — Team Inheritance | Create token as non-admin without `team_id`; check response | `team_id` auto-set to user's team | ✅ |
| 3a — blocked flag | Create token, use it to make a bad request; check `GET /tokens/{id}/stats` | `blocked_requests > 0` | ✅ |
| 3b — Revoked logging | Revoke token, attempt 3 calls with revoked token; check stats | `total_requests >= 3`, `blocked_requests >= 3` | ✅ |

Unit tests: `pytest tests/unit/mcpgateway/routers/test_tokens.py tests/unit/mcpgateway/middleware/test_token_usage_middleware.py` → **100% pass**

Full suite: `pytest tests/unit/` → **694 passed, 15 skipped**, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure in `test_email_auth_service_admin_role_sync` (unrelated to changed files).

---

## 📐 MCP Compliance (if relevant)
- [x] Matches current MCP spec
- [x] No breaking change to MCP clients

---

## ✅ Checklist
- [x] Code formatted (`make black isort pre-commit`)
- [x] No secrets/credentials committed

---

- tests/unit/mcpgateway/test_admin.py (line 8827): Added test `test_admin_gateways_partial_html_default_includes_inactive()` to verify gateways show inactive by default

- Tests fail without the fix: Both new tests fail with `AssertionError: Expected include_inactive default to be True, but got False`
- Tests pass with the fix applied

pr_title: fix(ui): pagination Next Page shows blank table after search
problem_statement:
## 📌 Summary
Clicking **Next Page** in any Admin UI table after a search (Tools, Gateways, Resources, Prompts, Servers, A2A Agents) produces a blank/broken table instead of showing the next page of results. This breaks pagination entirely whenever search results span more than one page.

## 🔗 Related Issue
Closes #3394 

## 🐞 Root Cause
`pagination_controls.html` defaults `swapStyle` to `innerHTML` when no `hx_swap` variable is set by the caller. After the first search, `loadSearchablePanel()` replaces `<div id="tools-table">` (a wrapper div) with `<table id="tools-table">` via `outerHTML` swap. From that point on, `loadPage()` fires `htmx.ajax` with `swap: 'innerHTML'` targeting `<table id="tools-table">`. An `innerHTML` swap on a `<table>` with a response body that starts with `<table>` produces invalid nested HTML — the browser automatically ejects the inner table as a sibling, leaving the visible table empty.

The bug affects all six entity tables: Tools, Servers, Resources, Prompts, Gateways, A2A Agents.

## 🔁 Reproducing the bug

I have added 50+ tools with the name pattern "search-repro-....", when I try searching with the keyword 'search', it should show more pages but the next pages aren't loading.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4679f6b4-b8b3-46b6-be2a-33f6012b7c2c


## 💡 Fix Description
Added `{% set hx_swap = 'outerHTML' %}` before `{% include 'pagination_controls.html' %}` in the OOB pagination block of each of the six affected partial templates. This sets `swapStyle: 'outerHTML'` in the Alpine component at render time, so `loadPage()` correctly replaces the entire `<table>` element rather than setting its inner HTML.

Key design points:
- The fix is in the partial templates only — `pagination_controls.html` itself is unchanged and remains `innerHTML` by default for callers with non-table targets (e.g. tokens, which targets a `<div>`).
- The pagination controls `<div>` is a sibling of the table, not inside it, so `outerHTML` swap never destroys the controls.
- `loadSearchablePanel()` always uses `outerHTML` explicitly — unaffected.
- The OOB `hx-swap-oob` mechanism is independent of `swapStyle` — unaffected.

## 🧪 Verification

| Check | Command | Status |
|---------------------------------------|----------------------|--------|
| Lint suite | `make lint` | Pass |
| Unit tests | `make test` | Pass |
| Coverage ≥ 90 % | `make coverage` | Pass |
| Manual: search 55+ tools → click Next Page → page 2 loads | Browser — Tools tab | Pass |
| Manual: search 55+ gateways → click Next Page → page 2 loads | Browser — Gateways tab | Pass |
| Manual: page size change still works after outerHTML swap | Browser — change to 10/page | Pass |
| Manual: tokens Next Page still works (innerHTML, unchanged) | Browser — Tokens tab | Pass |

## 📐 MCP Compliance (if relevant)
- [x] Matches current MCP spec
- [x] No breaking change to MCP clients

## ✅ Checklist
- [x] Code formatted (`make black isort pre-commit`)
- [x] No secrets/credentials committed

problem_statement:
## 🔗 Related Issue
Closes #3365 

  ---
  📝 Summary

  _execute_forwarded_request() now gates on HTTP status code before parsing the response body. Non-2xx       
  responses with non-JSON-RPC bodies (e.g. 401 {"detail":"..."}) are mapped to JSON-RPC errors instead of    
  silently returning {"result": {}}. The two session-affinity tests that depended on localhost port state are
   now hermetic via mocked HTTP responses, and two new test cases cover the non-2xx error mapping paths.     

 ---

  ## 🏷️ Type of Change
  - [x] Bug fix
  - [ ] Feature / Enhancement
  - [ ] Documentation
  - [ ] Refactor
  - [ ] Chore (deps, CI, tooling)

  | Check                     | Command         | Status |
  |---------------------------|-----------------|--------|
  | Lint suite                | `make lint`     | ✅     |
  | Unit tests                | `make test`     | ✅     |

  - [x] Code formatted (`make black isort pre-commit`)
  - [x] Tests added/updated for changes

  _execute_forwarded_request()

  test_execute_forwarded_request_returns_error_on_non_2xx_non_jsonrpc and

pr_title: fix(sse): use loopback for internal RPC calls in session registry
problem_statement:
## Summary

- Replace client-facing `base_url` with `http://127.0.0.1:{settings.port}/rpc` for internal self-calls in `generate_response()`, consistent with existing loopback patterns in `mcp_session_pool.py` and `streamablehttp_transport.py`
- Remove the `base_url` parameter from `respond()` and `generate_response()` along with the URL-parsing logic (`urlparse`, path extraction)
- Fix integration test to use `try/finally` for reliable cleanup and patch `settings.port` to match the mock RPC server

## Motivation

When the gateway is behind a reverse proxy or service mesh, the client-facing URL is not reachable from the server itself, causing internal RPC calls to fail. Using loopback avoids this issue.

Closes #3049

## Test plan

- [ ] Unit tests updated to remove `base_url` parameter from all `respond()` and `generate_response()` call sites
- [ ] `test_generate_response_uses_loopback_url` verifies the constructed URL is `http://127.0.0.1:{settings.port}/rpc`
- [ ] Integration test (`test_redis_broadcast_integration`) patches `settings.port` to match mock RPC server and uses `try/finally` for cleanup
- [ ] Deleted obsolete `TestGenerateResponseServersPath` tests that covered removed URL-parsing logic

## 🔗 Related Issue
Closes https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/issues/3233

---

## 📝 Summary

### Fix mcpgateway/services/mcp_client_chat_service.py

- Added `None` guard for `create_react_agent` in `MCPChatService.initialize()`
- Added `None` guard for `create_react_agent` in `MCPChatService.reload_tools()`
- Both raise `RuntimeError("Some dependencies are missing")` instead of the cryptic `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not callable`

### Tests

- test_initialize_raises_when_create_react_agent_is_none — patches `create_react_agent` to None, asserts `RuntimeError` and that `is_initialized` remains False
- test_reload_tools_raises_when_create_react_agent_is_none — same guard verified for `reload_tools()`
---

problem_statement:
# 🐛 Bug-fix PR

## 📌 Summary
Fixes intermittent `RuntimeError: Stream consumed` when admin form submissions are processed with detailed request logging enabled.

## 🔁 Reproduction Steps
Issue: #3313

1. Enable detailed request logging (`LOG_LEVEL=INFO` or lower).
2. Submit server form data from Admin UI (`/admin/servers`), especially with select-all style payloads.
3. Endpoint may fail while parsing `await request.form()` due to consumed request stream.

## 🐞 Root Cause
`RequestLoggingMiddleware` read `await request.body()` and then created a synthetic `Request` object (`new_request`) before calling `call_next`. Under `BaseHTTPMiddleware`, downstream processing uses the original ASGI receive channel, so reconstructing `Request` this way can leave downstream form parsing on a consumed stream.

## 💡 Fix Description
- Removed synthetic `Request` reconstruction in `request_logging_middleware`.
- Cached the body on the original request (`request._body = body`).
- Called `call_next(request)` with the original request object.
- Added regression coverage:
  - middleware pipeline/form parsing regression test
  - deterministic guard asserting the original request object is passed to `call_next`
  - admin-path form regression test under logging-enabled middleware

Closes #3313

pr_title: feat(rbac): enforce server_id scoping in /rpc endpoint for server-scoped tokens
problem_statement:
## Summary

Wires up the existing (but previously unused) `validate_server_access()` utility into the `/rpc` JSON-RPC handler so that server-scoped tokens can only operate on the server they are scoped to.


## Related Issue
Closes #2743

## Problem

The `TokenScopingMiddleware` enforces `scopes.server_id` for REST endpoints by matching URL paths (e.g. `/servers/{id}/tools`). However, `/rpc` is a multiplexed JSON-RPC handler where `server_id` is supplied in the **request body** (`params.server_id`), not the URL. This meant a token scoped to `server_id: "abc"` could POST to `/rpc` with `params.server_id: "xyz"` and be allowed through.

## Changes

### `mcpgateway/main.py`
- Imports `validate_server_access` from `mcpgateway/utils/token_scoping`.
- In `handle_rpc()`, after extracting `server_id` from params, extracts the JWT payload from `request.state._jwt_verified_payload` (stored as a `(token, payload)` tuple) and calls `validate_server_access(token_scopes, server_id)`.
- Returns a `403` HTTP response with a JSON-RPC `{"code": -32600}` error body when the token is scoped to a different server.
- The check is skipped when no `server_id` is present in params, preserving existing behaviour for global/unscoped calls.

### `tests/unit/mcpgateway/test_rpc_tool_invocation.py`
Adds `TestRPCServerIdScoping` with 5 tests:
- HTTP-level `403` returned when `validate_server_access` returns `False`.
- `validate_server_access` is **not** called when `server_id` is absent from params.
- Correct unpacking of `_jwt_verified_payload` tuple.
- Graceful handling of `None` payload (basic auth / no JWT → empty scopes → full access).
- Graceful handling of a JWT payload missing the `scopes` key → no restriction.

## Acceptance Criteria

| Criterion | Status |
|---|---|
| Server-scoped token (`server_id: "abc"`) rejected for `params.server_id: "xyz"` | ✅ |
| Server-scoped token (`server_id: "abc"`) allowed for `params.server_id: "abc"` | ✅ |
| Global tokens (no `scopes.server_id`) work for all servers | ✅ |
| Unit tests cover the new validation path | ✅ |
| Existing token scoping tests pass | ✅ |

problem_statement:
# 🐛 Bug-fix PR

Closes #3296

---

## Summary
Fixes broken admin redirects, template URLs, and UI cookie paths in proxy/embedded deployments where `request.scope["root_path"]` is empty but `settings.app_root_path` is configured. Follow-up to #3290 which only fixed the CSRF cookie path.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Set `APP_ROOT_PATH=/api/proxy/mcp` and deploy behind a proxy that does not populate ASGI `scope["root_path"]`.
2. Open Admin UI and perform any POST action (create gateway, delete tool, toggle state).
3. Observe redirect lands on `/admin#...` instead of `/api/proxy/mcp/admin#...`.

## Root Cause
The fix in #3290 introduced a fallback from `scope["root_path"]` to `settings.app_root_path` only in `_admin_cookie_path`. However, ~100 other call sites in `mcpgateway/admin.py` still read `request.scope.get("root_path", "")` directly:
- All `_build_admin_redirect()` callers (redirect URLs after POST actions)
- All template context dictionaries (rendered navigation, pagination, asset links)
- UI visibility cookie path construction
- `_request` variant handlers

These all produce incorrect paths in the same proxy deployment scenario.

## Fix Description
- **Extracted `_resolve_root_path(request)`**: A new helper that encapsulates the resolution logic — checks `scope["root_path"]` first, falls back to `settings.app_root_path`, normalizes (leading `/`, no trailing `/`).
- **Refactored `_admin_cookie_path`**: Now delegates to `_resolve_root_path` instead of inlining the logic.
- **Updated all call sites**: Replaced all `request.scope.get("root_path", "")` occurrences with `_resolve_root_path(request)` (or `_resolve_root_path(_request) if _request else ""` for nullable request variants).

## Verification

| Check                                 | Command              | Status |
|---------------------------------------|----------------------|--------|
| Targeted tests (10)                   | `uv run pytest -k "resolve_root_path or admin_cookie_path"` | 10 passed |
| Full admin test suite                 | `uv run pytest tests/unit/mcpgateway/test_admin.py` | 901 passed |

## Files Changed

| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `mcpgateway/admin.py` | Added `_resolve_root_path()` helper; replaced ~100 direct `scope["root_path"]` reads |
| `tests/unit/mcpgateway/test_admin.py` | Added 5 unit tests for `_resolve_root_path` |

## Checklist
- [x] Code formatted (`make black isort pre-commit`)
- [x] No secrets/credentials committed
- [x] Existing tests pass (901/901)
- [x] New tests cover helper behavior (5 tests)

problem_statement:
Signed-off-by: NAYANA.R <nayana.r7813@gmail.com>

closes #3051 
Implemented full fix for parameterized MIME handling in validation logic: accepts valid MIME parameters and still rejects malformed/unsafe formats in validators.py.

Updated admin UX guidance for UI resources so MIME helper text is contextual (shown for ui:// resource flows on MIME focus) in admin.html and admin.js.

Added and refined unit coverage for MIME validation in test_validators_advanced.py.

Added and refined e2e coverage for admin resource create/list persistence of parameterized MIME values in test_admin_apis.py.

Removed profile-specific example bias from docs/tests and generalized cases to avoid single hardcoded MIME dependencies.

+        """Test admin resource create/list accepts and persists parameterized MIME types."""
+        accepted_mime_types = [
+            "text/plain; charset=utf-8",
+            "application/json; charset=utf-8",
+            "text/html; profile=interactive-app",

+        created_resources: list[tuple[str, str]] = []

+            resource_uri = f"ui://resource-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"
+
+            form_data = {
+                "uri": resource_uri,

pr_title: [FIX][API] Token name uniqueness conflict returns generic 409 and admin UI freezes on backend errors
problem_statement:
# 🐛 Bug-fix PR

## 📌 Summary

Fixes a deterministic silent `409` when creating a token whose name already exists for the same user within the same team scope, and adds graceful error handling to the Admin UI team selector and token table for transient backend failures (DB pool exhaustion / idle transaction timeouts).

The DB constraint enforces name uniqueness per `(user_email, name, team_id)` — scoped per team — so the same token name is allowed across different teams but blocked within the same team scope. The service pre-check, router error handlers, and error formatter are all aligned to this model.

## 🔗 Related Issue

Closes #3229.

## 🐞 Root Cause

1. **Service layer** (`mcpgateway/services/token_catalog_service.py`) — `create_token()` duplicate pre-check did not correctly mirror the DB constraint, allowing duplicates to bypass the service check, hit the DB constraint, and bubble up as the opaque generic message `Unable to complete the operation. Please try again.`

2. **Router** (`mcpgateway/routers/tokens.py`) — Neither `POST /tokens` nor `POST /tokens/teams/{team_id}` caught `IntegrityError`. On a race-path duplicate the exception fell through to the global handler, producing a generic opaque message with no actionable detail.

3. **Error formatter** (`mcpgateway/utils/error_formatter.py`) — The token-specific message was nested inside an outer `if "UNIQUE constraint failed"` block that only covers SQLite errors, meaning PostgreSQL deployments (which report the constraint name, not the column path) were not matched. The Alembic migration constraint alias `uq_email_api_tokens_user_email_name` was also not handled.

4. **Admin UI** (`mcpgateway/static/admin.js`, `mcpgateway/templates/admin.html`) — Team selector used `htmx.ajax()` which silently ignores HTTP 5xx responses, leaving the dropdown visually empty with no error or retry affordance. The token table had no HTMX error listener at all. Token creation errors were only surfaced via a toast notification that could be missed if the user had scrolled.

5. **PgBouncer / connection pool** (`docker-compose.yml`) — `CLIENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT` was too close to `DB_POOL_RECYCLE`, creating a race where SQLAlchemy could hand a connection back from the pool at the exact moment PgBouncer was closing it — causing `idle transaction timeout` errors and 500s under admin traffic bursts.

## 💡 Fix Description

**Service layer** — Pre-check query now mirrors the DB constraint exactly: `(user_email, name, team_id)`. The same token name is allowed across different teams but blocked within the same team scope (including the global no-team bucket).

**DB constraint + migration** — `EmailApiToken.__table_args__` uses `UniqueConstraint("user_email", "name", "team_id", name="uq_email_api_tokens_user_name_team")`. Alembic migration `d9e0f1a2b3c4` handles the transition using `batch_alter_table` (SQLite + PostgreSQL safe) with idempotent upgrade/downgrade.

**Router** — Added `except IntegrityError` handlers to both `create_token` and `create_team_token`. Both catch all four constraint name variants:

- `uq_email_api_tokens_user_name_team` (new ORM / `db.py`)
- `uq_email_api_tokens_user_name` (legacy ORM)
- `uq_email_api_tokens_user_email_name` (Alembic migration)
- `email_api_tokens.user_email` + `email_api_tokens.name` column path (SQLite)

Returns HTTP 409 with a specific, user-actionable message instead of falling through to the global generic handler.

**Error formatter** — Token constraint check moved ahead of the generic `UNIQUE constraint failed` block so it always takes priority. Single clean `if` covering all four constraint name variants.

**Admin UI**
- Migrated `loadTeams()` in `admin.html` and `performTeamSelectorSearch()` in `admin.js` from `htmx.ajax()` to `fetch()` — both now detect HTTP 5xx and render an inline error with a Retry button. On failure, `dataset.loaded` is cleared (`delete container.dataset.loaded`) so reopening the dropdown automatically retries.
- Added `htmx:responseError` and `htmx:sendError` listeners on the tokens panel with an inline error + Retry in the token table.
- Added `<div id="token-creation-messages">` next to the create-token form that shows the API error inline on failure (auto-clears after 15 s) and is cleared on success.

**PgBouncer / pool** — Raised `CLIENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT` to 120 s in `docker-compose.yml`, making it 2× `DB_POOL_RECYCLE=60 s` so connections are always proactively recycled before PgBouncer closes them. Corrected misleading inline comments in `docker-compose-performance.yml`.

## 🧪 Verification

| Test | Command / Action | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Lint suite | `make lint` | ✅ |
| Unit tests | `make test` | ✅ 117 token / error-formatter tests pass |
| Coverage ≥ 90 % | `make coverage` | ✅ |
| Cross-scope duplicate → allowed | Create token N (no team), then N for a specific team | ✅ |
| Same-scope duplicate → specific 409 | Create identical name + team twice | ✅ |
| Race-path duplicate → specific 409 | `IntegrityError` injected via mock at router | ✅ |
| Team selector error + retry on 5xx | Simulate DB outage, open team dropdown | ✅ |
| Token table error + retry on 5xx | Simulate DB outage, navigate to Tokens panel | ✅ |
| Token form inline error on failure | Submit form with duplicate name | ✅ |

## 📐 MCP Compliance (if relevant)

- [x] Matches current MCP spec  
- [x] No breaking change to MCP clients

## ✅ Checklist

- [x] Code formatted (`make black isort pre-commit`)
- [x] No secrets/credentials committed

---

## 📝 Summary

Updated Ollama API configuration to use the native Ollama API endpoint `/api/tags` for listing models instead of the OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

Changes made:

### mcpgateway/db.py 

- Changed `api_base` from `http://localhost:11434/v1` to `http://localhost:11434`
- Changed `models_endpoint` from /`models` to `/api/tags`
- Updated description from "Local Ollama server (OpenAI-compatible)" to "Local Ollama server"

### mcpgateway/llm_provider_configs.py

- Changed `api_base_default` from `http://localhost:11434/v1` to `http://localhost:11434`
- Updated `api_base_help` from `Ollama server URL (use /v1 suffix for OpenAI compatibility)` to `Ollama server URL (native API)`
- Updated description to `Local Ollama server`

pr_title: [FEATURE][API]: Make tool description forbidden patterns configurable + fix auth_value encoding bug
problem_statement:
## Summary

- Add `TOOL_DESCRIPTION_FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS_ENABLED` (bool, default `true`) to disable all forbidden pattern checks on tool descriptions
- Add `TOOL_DESCRIPTION_FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS` (JSON array, default: original hardcoded list) to override the list of blocked substrings via env var
- Fix bug in `GatewayService._update_or_create_tools` where a dict `auth_value` was written directly to a `VARCHAR` column without encoding, causing a `psycopg.ProgrammingError` on gateway refresh/edit
- Expose both new settings in `docker-compose.yml` so they can be controlled per-deployment
- Add unit tests covering: default patterns block, disabled allows all, custom patterns, and None passthrough

## Related

Closes #3300

Fixes patterns in tool descriptions (e.g. query syntax documentation) being incorrectly blocked, and the 500 error when editing a gateway that has dict-typed auth headers.

@@ -844,6 +844,79 @@ def test_password_team_token_and_grpc_validators(monkeypatch):
     assert len(GrpcServiceUpdate.validate_description("x" * (SecurityValidator.MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH + 1))) == SecurityValidator.MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH
 
 
+class TestToolDescriptionForbiddenPatterns:
+    """Tests for configurable forbidden pattern validation on tool descriptions."""
+
+    def test_default_patterns_block_forbidden_chars(self, monkeypatch):
+        """Default forbidden patterns reject known unsafe substrings in strict mode."""
+        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "tool_description_forbidden_patterns_enabled", True)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "tool_description_forbidden_patterns", ["&&", ";", "||", "$(", "|", "> ", "< "])
+        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "validation_strict", True)
+        for pat in ["&&", ";", "||", "$(", "|", "> ", "< "]:
+            with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="unsafe characters"):
+                ToolCreate.validate_description(f"description with {pat} inside")
+
+    def test_non_strict_mode_warns_instead_of_rejecting(self, monkeypatch):
+        """When VALIDATION_STRICT=false, forbidden patterns produce a warning, not an error."""
+        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "tool_description_forbidden_patterns_enabled", True)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "tool_description_forbidden_patterns", ["&&", ";"])
+        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "validation_strict", False)
+        result = ToolCreate.validate_description("run && something")
+        assert result is not None
+
+    def test_disabled_allows_any_description(self, monkeypatch):
+        """Disabling forbidden patterns allows descriptions with any content."""
+        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "tool_description_forbidden_patterns_enabled", False)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "validation_strict", True)
+        result = ToolCreate.validate_description("run; rm -rf / && $(evil)")
+        assert result is not None
+
+    def test_custom_patterns_override_defaults(self, monkeypatch):
+        """Custom pattern list replaces the default list entirely."""
+        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "tool_description_forbidden_patterns_enabled", True)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "tool_description_forbidden_patterns", ["EVIL"])
+        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "validation_strict", True)
+        # Default patterns like ";" are no longer blocked
+        result = ToolCreate.validate_description("run; something")
+        assert ";" in result
+        # Custom pattern is blocked
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="unsafe characters"):
+            ToolCreate.validate_description("contains EVIL word")
+
+    def test_none_description_bypasses_check(self, monkeypatch):
+        """None descriptions are passed through without pattern checking."""
+        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "tool_description_forbidden_patterns_enabled", True)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "tool_description_forbidden_patterns", ["&&", ";"])
+        assert ToolCreate.validate_description(None) is None
+
+    def test_empty_pattern_in_list_does_not_match_everything(self, monkeypatch):
+        """Empty string patterns are filtered out and do not reject all descriptions."""
+        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "tool_description_forbidden_patterns_enabled", True)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "tool_description_forbidden_patterns", [""])
+        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "validation_strict", True)
+        # Empty pattern would match everything via `'' in v`; must be filtered
+        result = ToolCreate.validate_description("perfectly safe description")
+        assert result is not None
+
+
+class TestToolDescriptionForbiddenPatternsConfig:
+    """Tests for forbidden pattern config parsing and normalization."""
+
+    def test_filter_empty_forbidden_patterns(self):
+        """Empty/blank patterns are stripped from the config at validation time."""
+        from mcpgateway.config import Settings
+
+        s = Settings._filter_empty_forbidden_patterns(["&&", "", "  ", ";"])
+        assert s == ["&&", ";"]
+
+    def test_filter_preserves_valid_patterns(self):
+        """Non-empty patterns are preserved unchanged."""
+        from mcpgateway.config import Settings
+
+        patterns = ["&&", ";", "||", "$("]
+        assert Settings._filter_empty_forbidden_patterns(patterns) == patterns
+
+
 class TestMaskOauthConfig:
     """Tests for the _mask_oauth_config() helper function."""

pr_title: [FIX][UI]: Fix Alpine x-data parse error when query params contain double quotes
problem_statement:
# 🐛 Bug-fix PR

Closes #3261

---

## 📌 Summary
Fixes Alpine.js pagination components breaking whenever a server-side query parameter containing a double-quote character is embedded into an `x-data` attribute via Jinja's `tojson` filter. The most visible trigger is `team_id` when the gateway is used inside an iframe, but the same failure affects any user performing a free-text search (`q=foo"bar`) or any filter value that contains `"`.

## 🔁 Reproduction Steps

**Scenario A – iframe with team_id**
1. Embed the admin UI in an iframe: `<iframe src="http://localhost:4444/admin?team_id=<uuid>">`.
2. Open any paginated section — pagination controls fail to initialise.

**Scenario B – search with double quote (no iframe needed)**
1. Open the gateway admin UI directly.
2. In any paginated table, search for a term containing `"` (e.g. `foo"bar`).
3. Observe pagination controls stop working after the HTMX partial update.

## 🐞 Root Cause
`pagination_controls.html` embedded server-side query params directly into the Alpine `x-data` attribute using Jinja's `tojson` filter:

```jinja
url.searchParams.set({{ key | tojson | forceescape }}, {{ value | tojson | forceescape }});
```

`tojson` produces double-quoted JSON strings (`"team_id"`). Although `forceescape` converts `"` → `"` in the Jinja-rendered HTML, HTMX parses the partial response into DOM nodes during an OOB swap and re-serialises with `outerHTML`, converting `"` back to literal `"` before writing the updated `x-data` attribute into the page. The HTML parser then terminates the double-quoted `x-data` attribute at the first inner `"`, leaving Alpine with a truncated, unparseable expression.

All 10+ partial templates (`tools_partial.html`, `servers_partial.html`, `users_partial.html`, `tokens`, `prompts`, `resources`, `gateways`, `agents`, `teams`, `metrics`, `tools_with_pagination`) share `pagination_controls.html`, so all were affected. Vulnerable params by endpoint:

| Endpoint | Vulnerable params |
|---|---|
| `/admin/tools/partial` | `team_id`, `gateway_id`, `q`, `tags` |
| `/admin/servers/partial` | `q`, `relationship`, `visibility` |
| `/admin/tokens/partial` | `team_id`, `q` |
| All other paginated partials | `include_inactive` only (boolean — not vulnerable) |

## 💡 Fix Description
Move `query_params` out of the `x-data` JavaScript and into a dedicated `data-extra-params` HTML attribute, then read the values at runtime via `$el.dataset.extraParams`. Because the value sits in its own attribute it is never adjacent to the `x-data` attribute delimiter, completely eliminating the escaping hazard across all rendering paths (initial page load, HTMX full swap, HTMX OOB swap).

**`pagination_controls.html`** — two changes:

1. Add `data-extra-params` attribute to the container `<div>`:
```jinja
data-extra-params="{{ query_params | default({}) | tojson | forceescape }}"
```

2. Replace the Jinja `{% for key, value in query_params.items() %}` block inside `x-data` with pure JavaScript:
```javascript
const extraParams = JSON.parse(this.$el.dataset.extraParams || '{}');
Object.entries(extraParams).forEach(([k, v]) => {
  if (k !== 'include_inactive' && v !== null && v !== undefined) {
    url.searchParams.set(k, String(v));
  }
});

// Also pick up team_id if the parent app injects it into the browser URL
// (e.g. when the gateway is embedded in an iframe).
const currentUrlParams = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
const teamIdFromUrl = currentUrlParams.get('team_id');
if (teamIdFromUrl && !extraParams.team_id) {
  url.searchParams.set('team_id', teamIdFromUrl);
}
```

The `x-data` expression now contains no dynamic string values that can conflict with the HTML attribute delimiter, making it safe for all param values and all rendering paths.

## 🧪 Verification

| Check | Command | Status |
|---------------------------------------|----------------------|--------|
| Lint suite | `make lint` | pass |
| Unit tests | `make test` | pass |
| Coverage ≥ 80 % | `make coverage` | pass |
| Manual: search with `"` | Search `foo"bar` in any table, confirm pagination still works after HTMX swap | pass |

## 📐 MCP Compliance (if relevant)
- [x] Matches current MCP spec
- [x] No breaking change to MCP clients

## ✅ Checklist
- [x] Code formatted (`make black isort pre-commit`)
- [x] No secrets/credentials committed

pr_title: fix: 3014 - Postman import ignores API Key "in" placement setting and defaults to header
problem_statement: ### Description Postman import ignores API Key "in" placement setting and defaults to header Jira link - https://usebruno.atlassian.net/browse/BRU-3014 Postman's API Key auth supports two placements via the `in` field (`"header"` or `"query"`), but Bruno's Postman importer was ignoring that field entirely and hard-coding the placement to `"header"`. As a result, any Postman collection that authenticated by sending the API key as a query parameter would import incorrectly — the key/value were preserved, but the placement silently flipped to header, breaking the request. The fix is in `packages/bruno-converters/src/postman/postman-to-bruno.js`: when processing `APIKEY` auth, the converter now reads `authValues.in` and maps `"query"` to Bruno's `"queryparams"` placement, falling back to `"header"` for `"header"`, missing, or unknown values (which preserves the previous default for collections that don't specify `in`). Two Playwright tests were added under `tests/import/postman/` covering both placements end-to-end — importing a fixture collection, opening the imported request, and asserting that the Auth tab's placement dropdown reflects the original Postman setting. Before: After: #### Contribution Checklist: - [ ] **I've used AI significantly to create this pull request** - [x] **The pull request only addresses one issue or adds one feature.** - [x] **The pull request does not introduce any breaking changes** - [x] **I have added screenshots or gifs to help explain the change if applicable.** - [x] **I have read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/blob/main/contributing.md).** - [x] **Create an issue and link to the pull request.** Note: Keeping the PR small and focused helps make it easier to review and merge. If you have multiple changes you want to make, please consider submitting them as separate pull requests. #### Publishing to New Package Managers Please see [here](../publishing.md) for more information. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Postman collection import now preserves API key placement — imports API keys as query params or headers according to the source collection (no longer always headers). * **Tests** * Added end-to-end and unit tests validating Postman API key import and that the Auth UI shows correct placement after import. * **Chores** * Added test-friendly attributes and updated locators for import flows, modals, and API key placement UI to improve UI test reliability. pr_title: Fix 1086: Even after clearing the response, the test count keeps on displaying on the tests tab
problem_statement: ### Description [JIRA](https://usebruno.atlassian.net/browse/BRU-1086) Clear assertion and test results when response is cleared When a response is cleared in the Redux store, the associated test results (`assertionResults`, `preRequestTestResults`, and `postRequestTestResults`) are now also cleared along with response. This ensures consistency in the application state by preventing stale test results from being displayed alongside a cleared response. **Why this change:** - Prevents confusing UI state where old test results remain visible after clearing a response - Maintains consistency between response state and its related test results - Ensures clean state management when users clear/reset requests #### Contribution Checklist: - [ ] **I've used AI significantly to create this pull request** - [x] **The pull request only addresses one issue or adds one feature.** - [x] **The pull request does not introduce any breaking changes** - [x] **I have added screenshots or gifs to help explain the change if applicable.** - [x] **I have read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/usebruno/bruno/blob/main/contributing.md).** - [x] **Create an issue and link to the pull request.** Before: After fix: ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Clearing a response now also removes all associated test and runner results so no leftover test results persist. * **Tests** * Added end-to-end test validating response clearing resets test counters. * Added test helper utilities to insert pre-request, post-response, and test scripts for E2E scenarios.

pr_title: fix(collection-watcher): prevent crash when deleting collections
problem_statement:
### Description

- Fix uncaught "No collection configuration found" errors when deleting a collection that has OpenAPI sync configured
- Add fs.existsSync(collectionPath) guards to the change, unlink, and unlinkDir chokidar event handlers

[JIRA](https://usebruno.atlassian.net/browse/BRU-2862)

### Problem
When deleting an OpenAPI-synced collection, saveBrunoConfig() writes to bruno.json which creates buffered chokidar events (due to awaitWriteFinish with 80ms stability threshold). If the collection directory is removed before those buffered events fire, getCollectionFormat() throws "No collection configuration found" — once per .bru file in the collection.

This PR helps to persists scroll positions across tab switches for all request pane, response pane, folder settings, and collection settings tabs

pr_title: feat: add PropertyList API for req.headers and res.headers
problem_statement:
[Jira](https://usebruno.atlassian.net/browse/BRU-2893)

## Summary

Adds a `headerList` property to both `req` and `res` in scripts, exposing a structured PropertyList API for header management. Method names are aligned with the [MDN Web API Headers](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Headers) interface. The existing `req.headers` and `res.headers` raw objects remain untouched for full backward compatibility.

### New API

**`req.headerList`** — writable `HeaderList` (extends `PropertyList`, dynamic mode):
```js
// Read
req.headerList.get('Content-Type')              // 'application/json'
req.headerList.has('Authorization')             // true
req.headerList.one('Content-Type')              // { key: 'Content-Type', value: 'application/json' }
req.headerList.all()                            // [{ key, value }, ...]
req.headerList.count()                          // 3

// Search
req.headerList.find(h => h.key.startsWith('X-'))
req.headerList.filter(h => h.value.includes('json'))
req.headerList.indexOf('Content-Type')

// Iteration
req.headerList.forEach((h, i) => { ... })
req.headerList.map(h => h.key)
req.headerList.reduce((acc, h) => ..., {})

// Transform
req.headerList.toObject()                       // { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ... }
req.headerList.toString()                       // 'Content-Type: application/json\n...'

// Write
req.headerList.append({ key: 'X-Custom', value: 'val' })
req.headerList.append('X-Custom: val')          // string format
req.headerList.append('X-Custom', 'val')        // two-arg form
req.headerList.set({ key: 'Content-Type', value: 'text/plain' })
req.headerList.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain') // two-arg form
req.headerList.delete('X-Custom')
req.headerList.delete(h => h.key.startsWith('X-'))
req.headerList.clear()
req.headerList.populate([{ key: 'A', value: '1' }, ...])
req.headerList.repopulate([{ key: 'A', value: '1' }])
req.headerList.assimilate(otherList, true)
```

**`res.headerList`** — read-only `HeaderList` (static mode, write methods throw):
```js
res.headerList.get('content-type')              // 'application/json'
res.headerList.has('x-request-id')              // true
res.headerList.all()                            // [{ key, value }, ...]
res.headerList.filter(h => h.key.startsWith('x-'))
res.headerList.toObject()                       // plain object map
```

### Key design decisions

- **Separate property**: `req.headerList` / `res.headerList` is distinct from `req.headers` / `res.headers` — no Proxy layer, no risk of breaking existing scripts
- **MDN-aligned naming**: Write methods use `append`, `set`, `delete`, `forEach` (matching [MDN Headers](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Headers))
- **Case-insensitive**: All key lookups are case-insensitive (HTTP headers are case-insensitive)
- **Disabled headers**: `req.headerList` surfaces disabled headers with `{ disabled: true }` — users can query/filter them
- **Dynamic reads**: `req.headerList` reads from the live `req.headers` object on every access, so mutations via `req.setHeader()` are always reflected
- **QuickJS support**: Full PropertyList bridge wired into the QuickJS sandbox with iterator support and synchronous write hooks

### `append` vs MDN's `Headers.append()`

MDN's `append()` creates duplicate headers with the same key. Bruno does not support multiple headers with the same name, so `append()` delegates to `set()` — it overwrites any existing header with the same key.

### `populate` and `repopulate`

- **`populate(items)`** — Adds headers from the array/string, but **skips any key that already exists** (case-insensitive). Postman's `populate` adds duplicate keys because Postman supports multiple headers with the same name. Bruno does not, so we skip existing keys to preserve the current value.
- **`repopulate(items)`** — Clears all existing headers first, then adds the new items. Matches Postman's `repopulate` behavior.

---

## Complete API Reference

All key lookups are **case-insensitive** per the HTTP spec.

### `req.headerList` — Request Headers (read-write)

#### Read Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `get(name)` | `string \| undefined` | Value of the first header matching the key |
| `one(name)` | `object \| undefined` | Full header object `{ key, value }` for the matching key |
| `all()` | `object[]` | Cloned array of all header objects `{ key, value, disabled? }` |
| `count()` | `number` | Number of headers (including disabled) |

#### Search Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `has(name)` | `boolean` | `true` if a header with that key exists |
| `has(name, value)` | `boolean` | `true` if key exists **and** value matches exactly |
| `has(object)` | `boolean` | `true` if a header with `object.key` exists |
| `find(fn, context?)` | `object \| undefined` | First header where the predicate returns truthy |
| `filter(fn, context?)` | `object[]` | All headers where the predicate returns truthy |
| `indexOf(item)` | `number` | Index of a header by string key or `{ key, value }` object; `-1` if not found |

#### Iteration Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `forEach(fn, context?)` | `void` | Calls `fn(header, index)` for every header |
| `map(fn, context?)` | `any[]` | Returns a new array of mapped values |
| `reduce(fn, initial?, context?)` | `any` | Reduces headers to a single value |

#### Transform Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `toObject(excludeDisabled?, caseSensitive?, multiValue?, sanitizeKeys?)` | `object` | Plain `{ key: value }` map |
| `toString()` | `string` | HTTP wire format `Key: Value\n...` (skips disabled headers) |
| `toJSON()` | `object[]` | Same as `all()` — suitable for `JSON.stringify()` |

#### Write Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `append(headerObj \| name, value?)` | `void` | Sets a header; accepts `{ key, value }`, `"Key: Value"` string, or `(name, value)` two-arg form. Delegates to `set()` (overwrites existing). |
| `set(headerObj \| name, value?)` | `boolean \| null` | Sets or replaces a header. Returns `true` if new, `false` if updated, `null` if input was nil. |
| `delete(predicate, context?)` | `void` | Deletes header(s) by key string, `{ key }` object, or predicate function |
| `clear()` | `void` | Removes **all** headers (enabled and disabled) |
| `populate(items \| string)` | `void` | Adds items from array or multi-line string, **skipping keys that already exist** |
| `repopulate(items \| string)` | `void` | Clears all headers, then populates with new items |
| `assimilate(source, prune?)` | `void` | Merges headers from a PropertyList or array; if `prune` is true, removes headers not present in source |

---

### `res.headerList` — Response Headers (read-only)

All write methods (`append`, `set`, `delete`, `clear`, `populate`, `repopulate`, `assimilate`) throw a `"HeaderList is read-only"` error when called on response headers.

#### Read Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `get(name)` | `string \| undefined` | Value of the first header matching the key |
| `one(name)` | `object \| undefined` | Full header object `{ key, value }` for the matching key |
| `all()` | `object[]` | Cloned array of all header objects `{ key, value }` |
| `count()` | `number` | Number of headers |

#### Search Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `has(name)` | `boolean` | `true` if a header with that key exists |
| `has(name, value)` | `boolean` | `true` if key exists **and** value matches exactly |
| `has(object)` | `boolean` | `true` if a header with `object.key` exists |
| `find(fn, context?)` | `object \| undefined` | First header where the predicate returns truthy |
| `filter(fn, context?)` | `object[]` | All headers where the predicate returns truthy |
| `indexOf(item)` | `number` | Index of a header by string key or `{ key, value }` object; `-1` if not found |

#### Iteration Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `forEach(fn, context?)` | `void` | Calls `fn(header, index)` for every header |
| `map(fn, context?)` | `any[]` | Returns a new array of mapped values |
| `reduce(fn, initial?, context?)` | `any` | Reduces headers to a single value |

#### Transform Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `toObject(excludeDisabled?, caseSensitive?, multiValue?, sanitizeKeys?)` | `object` | Plain `{ key: value }` map |
| `toString()` | `string` | HTTP wire format `Key: Value\n...` |
| `toJSON()` | `object[]` | Same as `all()` — suitable for `JSON.stringify()` |
